messages:
incident-bot: ALERT — GeoDNS resolver error spike detected for eu-west-1 customers. (>5xx rate) auto-paged sre-oncall.

maya: i'm seeing 5xxs across multiple services in eu-west-1b; looks like DNS answers are sometimes returning old origins causing traffic to go to a decommissioned AZ egress path. customers hitting model inference most affected.

jamal: confirmed. traces show ~30% of requests to eu endpoints getting NX or stale A records then timing out -> 503 from edge.

sre-oncall: paging in, collecting impact. can someone check route53 health checks + cloudflare analytics? suspecting propagation / resolver cache mismatch.

netops-santiago: on it. quick note: we rolled the NAT gateway pool in eu-west-1 last night (SNAT migration) and a subset had a misconfigured egress ACL. could explain asymmetric responses from some resolvers.

maya: here's a rapid repro from my laptop (eu vpn):

```
curl -I https://inference.api.redwood.internal/health -H "Host: inference.redwood.ai"
# sometimes 200, sometimes 503
HTTP/2 503

# dig to two public resolvers in eu:
; dig +short @1.1.1.1 inference.redwood.ai A
54.36.12.5
54.36.12.5
; dig +short @4.4.4.4 inference.redwood.ai A
52.47.99.1
```

jamal: weird — different resolvers returning different origin IPs. TTL shown as 300 on some, 60 on others. could be a stale zone in Route53 replication or Cloudflare cached record mismatch.

netops-santiago: i see BGP flap logs around the time of NAT migration; some egress paths were withdrawn briefly. route53 health checks for eu-prod were flapping too (showing unhealthy during withdraw).

sre-oncall: mitigation plan (short):
1) reduce Route53 record TTLs to 60 for affected names (immediate but careful)
2) shift GeoDNS weight away from eu-west-1b -> eu-west-1a/backup POP via change-batch (temporary)
3) ask Cloudflare to purge DNS cache for the zone and escalate to support if CF edges hold stale answers
4) put automatic fallback routing in smart-router to direct traffic to dedicated capacity in other regions for flagged customers

cloud-eng-alex: preparing a Route53 change-batch now. change JSON includes weight adjustment + TTL update. command i'm going to run:

```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z02345EXAMPLE --change-batch file://route53-change.json
```

sre-oncall: please hold on executing until we confirm read-only maintenance window? this is high-severity but non-destructive. proceed with low-risk changes (TTL + weight) only.

netops-santiago: i've opened a ticket with Cloudflare (TICKET-45781) and flagged as P1. CF edge logs show cached A answers with old origin for ~12% of queries. asked them to purge immediately.

lina-product: customer impact — we have reports from two enterprise customers in eu with increased 503s and request timeouts. product-support is drafting a status message; recommend telling them: intermittent service degradation in eu, engineers working on routing + DNS.

jamal: i'm seeing metrics improve after pushing route53 weight change and decreasing TTL (ran at +1719876650). 503 rate dropped from 18% -> 6% in 2 mins but still noisy.

sre-oncall: follow-up actions:
- continue monitoring resolver split (CF vs Route53) for next 30m
- keep TTL low for 6 hours, then incrementally roll back to 300 after stability window
- schedule a postmortem to dive into why NAT migration didn't fail-safe and why our healthcheck flapping didn't trigger automated failover earlier
- update incident channel and customer status page

maya: ops notes added to incident doc. quick snippet of the change we applied: 

```
route53-change.json (excerpt):
{
  "Changes": [
    {
      "Action": "UPSERT",
      "ResourceRecordSet": {
        "Name": "inference.redwood.ai",
        "Type": "A",
        "SetIdentifier": "eu-west-1b-temporary",
        "Weight": 10,
        "TTL": 60,
        "ResourceRecords": [{"Value": "52.47.99.1"}]
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

netops-santiago: long term: we need a preflight for NAT/gateway egress changes that includes synthetic DNS/health checks from multiple public resolvers and an automatic route53 fallback if healthcheck latency > threshold.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied — Route53 weight changed, TTL lowered, Cloudflare purge requested. Service partial restoration observed.

sre-oncall: handing off to night oncall in 30m. summary to handoff: root cause likely egress ACL + NAT migration + resolver cache divergence (Route53 <-> Cloudflare). continued monitoring required for 4h.

lina-product: sending customer update: "We experienced intermittent failures for EU inference traffic. Engineers changed DNS routing and reduced DNS TTLs to restore service; we are continuing to monitor and will follow up with a detailed postmortem." :white_check_mark: 

jamal: after additional CF purge and another small weight shift, error-rate now 1.2% and trending down. leaving synthetic probes on.

sre-oncall: thanks all. tagging for postmortem: netops-santiago, cloud-eng-alex, jamal, maya. handing off now.

netops-santiago: noted — will pull NAT migration logs + BGP flaps for postmortem.

incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED (monitored): service restored to within SLA thresholds. postmortem ticket created: PM-8793.
